title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ross, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ross, ND
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Ross, ND, home to its own named Bakken field in Mountrail County? Get a straight, well-informed offer.
heroLead: Ross has its own named field in the Bakken, which tells you this stretch of Mountrail County has been drilled seriously, on its own merits rather than as spillover from a neighboring town.
intro: Ross field has been developed steadily since the mid-2000s, and families who held onto mineral rights from the original homestead-era ownership around here have generally seen real royalty income over the years, even if it's slowed as the wells matured. If you're one of them and you're weighing whether to keep collecting a shrinking monthly check or sell the interest outright, that's exactly the decision we help owners think through.

sections.heading: Ross field's place in the Bakken core
paragraphs: Ross sits solidly within Mountrail County's productive core, and wells here have generally performed in line with the rest of the county's strong track record. We check the specific wellbores tied to your spacing unit and their current production stage before we make an offer.

sections.heading: The keep-or-sell decision most owners face
paragraphs: A mature well still producing means you can keep collecting a declining monthly royalty for years, or sell now for a lump sum based on the well's remaining value. There's no universally right answer, it depends on your family's goals, and we'll walk through both honestly rather than push you toward selling.

sections.heading: Confirming title on Ross-area interests
paragraphs: Like most of Mountrail County, mineral rights near Ross were often divided among heirs over the decades without every transfer being formally recorded. We pull the county recorder's file to confirm the actual chain of title before we make an offer, so the number reflects your real, current ownership share.
If we find a gap between what's on file and what your family believes you own, we'll walk you through what's needed to fix it.

faqs.question: Is Ross field considered a strong part of the Bakken?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's a solidly productive part of Mountrail County's core acreage, with a track record going back to the mid-2000s.

faqs.question: Should we keep collecting royalties or sell now?
faqs.answer: It depends on your goals. A mature well can still pay for years, but the total tends to be a declining amount. We'll explain the tradeoffs honestly for your specific well.

faqs.question: How do you calculate what a declining well is worth today?
faqs.answer: We look at recent production trends, decline rate, and nearby activity to estimate remaining value, rather than pricing off historic peak production.

faqs.question: The county recorder's file doesn't match what we believe we own. What now?
faqs.answer: That's common with older heirship situations. We'll explain exactly what documentation is needed to bring the record in line with your family's actual ownership.
